create.name: Dana Ullman
create.bio:
Dana Ullman took his undergraduate degree at UC Berkeley in 1975 and a Master's in Public Health there afterwards, adding certification in classical homeopathy and a doctoral degree in homeopathy from the British Institute of Homeopathy. He has stayed in Berkeley ever since, where Homeopathic Educational Services — the company he founded and chairs — has operated out of a Camelia Street address for decades.

If the other figures in this cohort are teachers of practitioners, Ullman is the field's public advocate and archivist. He has written ten books, several of which — Everybody's Guide to Homeopathic Medicines, co-written with Stephen Cummings MD, and Homeopathic Medicine for Children and Infants — have been in print for more than thirty years and are the books most often handed to an English-speaking newcomer. The Homeopathic Revolution takes a different angle: it assembles the historical record of well-known figures who used homeopathy, from Darwin to Gandhi, and is the book he is best known for outside the field.

He chaired the National Center for Homeopathy's annual conference from 1986, wrote a long-running column for HuffPost, and now publishes on Substack. His current major project is Evidence Based Homeopathic Family Medicine, a 750-page ebook that indexes more than 500 clinical studies published in peer-reviewed journals, sold as a rolling subscription so it can be updated. He has also received a lifetime achievement award from within the profession. Of the five healers here, he is the one whose work is most concerned with argument, evidence and the historical record rather than with clinical method.

books.title: Everybody's Guide to Homeopathic Medicines
books.author: Stephen Cummings, Dana Ullman
books.description: The book that has introduced more English-speaking readers to homeopathy than any other, co-written with a physician and continuously in print for over three decades. Organised by everyday complaint, it is written as a household reference for people who want to understand what the remedies in a home kit are for.

books.title: The Homeopathic Revolution: Why Famous People and Cultural Heroes Choose Homeopathy
books.author: Dana Ullman
books.description: His best-known book, and the one that reads least like a manual. Ullman assembles the documentary record of writers, scientists, musicians, clergy and heads of state who used homeopathy — Darwin, Gandhi, Beethoven, Tolstoy among them — and argues that the history has been quietly written out. Foreword by Peter Fisher.

books.title: Discovering Homeopathy: Your Introduction to the Science and Art of Homeopathic Medicine
books.author: Dana Ullman
books.description: His longer-form introduction, setting out the history of the subject, the principles as he understands them, and the research literature as it stood. Widely used as a first text on introductory courses in the US.

books.title: Homeopathic Medicine for Children and Infants
books.author: Dana Ullman
books.description: His paediatric guide for parents, published by Tarcher and long established in the family-health section. Written in the same plain register as Everybody's Guide.

books.title: The Consumer's Guide to Homeopathy
books.author: Dana Ullman
books.description: Written for the reader deciding whether to engage with homeopathy at all — what it claims, how to find a practitioner, what to expect, and how to read the evidence. Practical in a consumer-advocacy sense rather than a clinical one.

books.title: Homeopathy: Medicine for the 21st Century
books.author: Dana Ullman
books.description: The UK edition of his introductory argument, published by Thorsons. Largely overlapping with Discovering Homeopathy but framed for a British readership.

books.title: The One-Minute (or So) Healer: 500 Quick and Simple Ways to Heal Yourself Naturally
books.author: Dana Ullman
books.description: A departure from his homeopathy writing — a collection of brief self-care practices drawn from a range of traditions, gathered with an eye for the wry and the quotable. The lightest book in his catalogue and the best fit for a general wellbeing audience.

books.title: The Steps to Healing: Wisdom from the Sages, the Rosemarys, and the Times
books.author: Dana Ullman
books.description: The companion to The One-Minute Healer, structured around quotations and reflections on what healing asks of a person. More contemplative than instructional.

books.title: Homeopathy and Self-Healing
books.author: Dana Ullman
books.description: A shorter title connecting his homeopathic work to the wider self-healing literature. Less circulated than his major books but directly on Spiritpedia's subject territory.

books.title: Essential Homeopathy: What It Is and What It Can Do for You
books.author: Dana Ullman
books.description: A brief primer published by New World Library, written as the shortest possible honest answer to "what is this?" for someone encountering the subject for the first time.

courses.title: Learning How to Use a Homeopathic Medicine Kit — an eCourse (80 videos)
courses.description: His flagship course — eighty videos taking a home user through the remedies in a standard homeopathic medicine kit, what he understands each to be indicated for, and how he approaches selection. Currently his site's headline product.

courses.title: Evidence Based Homeopathic Family Medicine — 2-year subscription
courses.description: The 750-page research ebook sold as a rolling two-year subscription, with updates issued at least twice a year as new studies are published. Positioned by Ullman as the most complete single source on the clinical research literature.

free_resources.title: Evidence Based Homeopathic Family Medicine — free 191-page sample
free_resources.description: An openly published PDF containing 191 pages of his 750-page research ebook — no signup, no account, just a direct download. This is the single most substantial free asset found across all five healers in this audit, and by a wide margin his best free offering.

free_resources.title: Dana Ullman on Substack
free_resources.description: Where he now publishes most actively — essays on the research literature, the history of the field, and his ongoing arguments with critics. Free posts are readable without subscribing.

free_resources.title: HuffPost author archive
free_resources.description: His long-running column, freely readable in full. Written for a mainstream readership rather than a homeopathic one, which makes it the most accessible entry point into his thinking.

free_resources.title: Introduction to Homeopathy — article archive
free_resources.description: A curated set of his introductory articles on his own site, sequenced for someone starting from nothing. Openly readable with no account.

free_resources.title: Homeopathic Research — article archive
free_resources.description: His collected writing on the research literature — study summaries, methodological arguments, and responses to critics — free and openly accessible.

free_resources.title: How To Learn Homeopathy — article archive
free_resources.description: His guidance on routes into studying the subject — what to read first, what training exists, and how he suggests a beginner sequences it.

free_resources.title: Homeopathic Educational Services blog
free_resources.description: The site's ongoing blog, carrying his longer posts and announcements. Overlaps with the category archives above but is the chronological feed.
